feedback: Confirm whether the chosen case genuinely makes the product NOT bigger than the starting number: either smaller (e.g. a positive starting number times a factor below 1, or times 0) or equal (e.g. × 1). Then ask the learner to articulate the reason.
Do not treat a correct selection as evidence that the learner can construct a proof chain or explain a flaw independently.
activities.intendedInsight: Recognising which case is a counter-example is a useful entry step, but choosing from options does not itself elicit a constructed proof or a flaw explained in one's own words.
learnerActions: From several candidate cases, pick the one that disproves a stated 'always' claim (e.g. which case breaks 'multiplying makes bigger'?).
After choosing, say aloud why that case is decisive and why the other candidates do not break the claim.
activities.title: Pick-the-breaker warm-up
